Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The captain said that they had been struggling to chase big scores.
options_en: The captain says, "We are struggling to chase big scores."
The captain said, "We are struggling to chase big scores."
The captain said, "We have been struggling to chase big scores."
The captain said, "We struggle to score big scores."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Perfect Continuous Tense.

Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had been + Present Participle + Object) will be converted into Present Perfect Continuous (Subject + has/have been + Present participle + Object).

For example:

He said that they had been waiting for hours. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "We have been waiting for hours" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:
Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
said thatsaid
had been strugglinghave been struggling
theyWe

From the given options, one that follows the above-mentioned conditions for Direct speech is option (c) "The captain said, "We have been struggling to chase big scores"."

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Rahul is writing an amazing essay. He is also solving the math problems.
options_en: An amazing essay was written by Rahul. The math problems have also been solved by him.
An amazing essay is being written by Rahul. The math problems are also being solved by him.
An amazing essay was written by Rahul. The math problems were also solved by him.
An amazing essay has been written by Rahul. He solved the math problems.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb ['being'] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "An amazing essay is being written by Rahul. The math problems are also being solved by him."

Hence, option (b) is correct.

The anchor of the programme asked us whether we were ready for a challenge.

"Are you ready for a challenge?" the anchor of the programme said to us.

questions.solution_en:
The main verb in the reported speech is 'asked', hence in the direct form, the reporting speech should be an interrogative sentence. Also the use of 'whether' clarifies that it should be a yes/no type question (also known as 'polar question') starting with an auxiliary verb ('have', 'do', 'be').

We see that the reported speech of the sentence is in simple past tense (past tense form 'were') so the direct form should be in simple present tense ('were' changes to 'are').

Option (a) is incorrect because of the (unnecessary) word 'this'.

The correct direct form is - ["Are you ready for a challenge?" the anchor of the programme said to us.]

The answer is option (c).

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

In China, there once lived a father, his four sons, and three daughters-in-law. His three older sons had married within a few months of each other and all with young women from the same village. Recently, these three new daughters-in-law had been brought into the house. Their new father-in-law's wife had died a few years before and having no mother-in-law with them in their new home, and being lonesome and homesick for their former families, they constantly asked the old man for permission to visit their former village. For you see, those were the days when young women, after they married and moved into the homes of their new husbands, needed permission to leave the household. Annoyed by the continual pleas of his three new daughters-in-law, the old father thought of a way to put an end to it.

He gave the young women permission in this way, saying, "You are always begging me to allow you to go and visit your mothers, and you think I am very hard-hearted for not letting you go. Now you may go, but only upon this condition. When you come back, you must each bring me something that I want. One of you must bring me some fire in paper, the other must bring me some wind in paper, and the third must bring me some music in wind. Unless you promise to bring me this, you are never to ask me to let you go home. And if you go and fail to get these for me, you are never to come back." The old man did not suppose that these conditions would be accepted. Of course, they were hard to understand, much less to fulfil. But the girls were young and thoughtless, and in their anxiety to get away did not consider any of that. So, they promised and made ready with speed. In great glee, they started off on foot to visit their mothers.

Which of the following questions cannot be answered on the basis of the above passage?
options_en: How many sons did the old man have?
Which son did not get married?
Where did the old man's daughters-in-law want to go?
Why did one of his sons not marry?
questions.solution_en:
The answer of option (a) is four (as given in the first paragraph of the passage).

The answer of option (b) is - the youngest one, as it's mentioned in the first paragraph of the passage that the three older sons were married.

The answer of option (c) is - their former village (as given in the first paragraph of the passage).

There's nowhere mentioned the reason why the youngest son wasn't married. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The answer of option (b) is - the youngest one, as it's mentioned in the first paragraph of the passage that the three older sons were married.

The answer of option (c) is - their former village (as given in the first paragraph of the passage).

There's nowhere mentioned the reason why the youngest son wasn't married. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate synonym for 'fatigued' is 'exhausted'.

'Fatigued' means extremely tired or worn out.

'Exhausted' also means very tired.

'Energetic' means full of energy.

'Careless' means not paying enough attention.

'Alert' means fully awake and aware.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.
